classified.text: The chief concern is primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain that acutely worsened.
classified.rationale: This states the presenting clinical problem and symptom pattern as an observable patient attribute.

classified.text: The patient is 25 years old.
classified.rationale: This is a numerical age claim that can be directly verified.

classified.text: The patient has never menstruated.
classified.rationale: This is a factual statement about the patient's menstrual history.

classified.text: The patient has normal secondary sexual development.
classified.rationale: This describes a patient characteristic that can be assessed clinically.

classified.text: Breast development occurred at age 11.
classified.rationale: This gives a specific age and is therefore a numerical claim.

classified.text: Pubic hair development occurred at age 12.
classified.rationale: This gives a specific age and is therefore a numerical claim.

classified.text: The patient is Tanner stage 4 for breasts and pubic hair.
classified.rationale: Tanner stage is a numeric clinical staging value.

classified.text: Normal secondary sexual development indicates functioning ovaries and estrogen exposure.
classified.rationale: This links a clinical finding to an inferred physiologic implication.

classified.text: The long history of dull cramping abdominal pain began at age 13.
classified.rationale: This includes a specific age of onset, making it a numerical claim.

classified.text: The abdominal pain became cyclic every 45–50 days by age 16.
classified.rationale: This contains specific timing and interval values.

classified.text: The pain pattern strongly suggests occult menstruation with outflow obstruction rather than endocrine failure.
classified.rationale: This asserts a mechanistic interpretation of the symptom pattern.

classified.text: The current 2-day episode involved sudden severe lower abdominal pain.
classified.rationale: This includes a specific duration and severity description tied to the episode.

classified.text: The current pain episode is likely an acute exacerbation related to retained menstrual blood in an obstructed reproductive tract.
classified.rationale: This proposes a cause-and-effect explanation for the acute pain.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include primary amenorrhea despite normal pubertal development.
classified.rationale: This summarizes observed positive clinical findings.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include cyclic abdominal pain for years.
classified.rationale: This is a factual summary of the symptom history.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include mild right lower quadrant tenderness.
classified.rationale: This reports an exam finding.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include ultrasound showing blood within the right uterine horn.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging finding.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include MRI showing a bicornuate likely unicollis uterus.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging interpretation.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include MRI showing a single angulated cervix.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging finding.

classified.text: Salient positive findings include MRI showing a blind upper half of the vagina.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging finding.

classified.text: These imaging findings point to a müllerian anomaly with distal obstruction.
classified.rationale: This interprets the imaging findings as indicating a specific anatomic mechanism.

classified.text: Blood in the uterine horn indicates hematometra from retained menses.
classified.rationale: This explains the meaning of the imaging finding in causal/pathophysiologic terms.

classified.text: A blind upper vagina suggests a transverse vaginal septum or segmental vaginal agenesis causing obstruction.
classified.rationale: This links the anatomic finding to a likely obstructive cause.

classified.text: The single cervix and bicornuate uterus support a complex obstructive müllerian malformation rather than isolated imperforate hymen.
classified.rationale: This compares findings and infers a more likely underlying mechanism.

classified.text: MRI also noted adenomyosis-like myometrial changes.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging observation.

classified.text: MRI also noted polycystic-appearing ovaries.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging observation.

classified.text: The adenomyosis-like myometrial changes and polycystic-appearing ovaries do not explain the lifelong primary amenorrhea with cyclic pain and obstructed blood collection.
classified.rationale: This states why those findings are not the cause of the main syndrome.

classified.text: She denied fever.
classified.rationale: This is a factual symptom denial.

classified.text: She denied vomiting.
classified.rationale: This is a factual symptom denial.

classified.text: She denied bowel symptoms.
classified.rationale: This is a factual symptom denial.

classified.text: She denied urinary symptoms.
classified.rationale: This is a factual symptom denial.

classified.text: These denials make appendicitis, urinary tract pathology, or gastrointestinal causes less likely.
classified.rationale: This infers diagnostic likelihood from the absence of symptoms.

classified.text: She is sexually inactive.
classified.rationale: This is a factual patient attribute.

classified.text: Sexual inactivity makes pregnancy-related causes very unlikely.
classified.rationale: This links sexual history to reduced likelihood of pregnancy.

classified.text: Sexual inactivity makes pelvic inflammatory disease very unlikely.
classified.rationale: This links sexual history to reduced likelihood of PID.

classified.text: Normal body habitus argues against gonadal dysgenesis.
classified.rationale: This uses a clinical feature to argue against a diagnosis.

classified.text: Normal secondary sexual characteristics argue against hypothalamic amenorrhea.
classified.rationale: This links pubertal development to diagnostic reasoning.

classified.text: Normal secondary sexual characteristics argue against androgen insensitivity.
classified.rationale: This links pubertal development to diagnostic reasoning.

classified.text: The presence of a uterus on imaging excludes Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome.
classified.rationale: This uses an anatomic finding to rule out a diagnosis.

classified.text: The cyclic pain and hematometra argue against PCOS as the primary explanation for amenorrhea.
classified.rationale: This explains why the symptom pattern is inconsistent with PCOS as the main cause.

classified.text: The ovaries appear polycystic.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging observation.

classified.text: Obstructive müllerian anomaly causing cryptomenorrhea is a candidate differential.
classified.rationale: This states a diagnostic possibility rather than a recommendation or mechanism.

classified.text: A transverse vaginal septum or upper vaginal obstruction with bicornuate unicollis uterus fits best.
classified.rationale: This asserts the best-fitting anatomic explanation for the findings.

classified.text: This fit is supported by primary amenorrhea, normal pubertal development, cyclic pain, blind upper vagina, single cervix, and blood in the uterine horn.
classified.rationale: This explains why the listed findings support the diagnosis.

classified.text: Cervical agenesis or dysgenesis with a functioning uterus is a candidate differential.
classified.rationale: This names a possible diagnosis.

classified.text: Cervical agenesis or dysgenesis can cause primary amenorrhea and cyclic pain with hematometra.
classified.rationale: This describes the mechanism by which the condition produces symptoms.

classified.text: MRI noted suboptimal visualization of the uterocervical junction.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging limitation/finding.

classified.text: A cervix was seen as a single angulated cervix.
classified.rationale: This reports an imaging finding.

classified.text: The blind upper vagina more directly supports vaginal-level obstruction rather than complete cervical agenesis.
classified.rationale: This compares findings and infers the more likely level of obstruction.

classified.text: Imperforate hymen is a candidate differential.
classified.rationale: This states a possible diagnosis.

classified.text: Imperforate hymen causes primary amenorrhea and cyclic pain from outflow obstruction.
classified.rationale: This describes the pathophysiologic relationship between the condition and symptoms.

classified.text: Imperforate hymen usually presents with a bulging hymen and distended vagina.
classified.rationale: This describes typical clinical features of the condition.

classified.text: Imperforate hymen usually presents with hematocolpos.
classified.rationale: This describes a typical associated finding.

classified.text: The imaging findings do not match a bulging hymen and distended vagina.
classified.rationale: This uses imaging to argue against the diagnosis.

classified.text: PCOS is a candidate differential.
classified.rationale: This states a possible diagnosis.

classified.rationale: This reports an imaging observation.

classified.text: The pain became cyclic at 45–50-day intervals.
classified.rationale: This gives a specific interval frequency.

classified.text: PCOS does not explain complete lifelong amenorrhea in the presence of retained blood in a uterine horn and an anatomic vaginal obstruction.
classified.rationale: This explains why PCOS is not the primary cause given the anatomic findings.

classified.text: Endometriosis is a candidate differential.
classified.rationale: This states a possible diagnosis.

classified.rationale: This reports an imaging impression.

classified.text: Chronic outflow obstruction can lead to endometriosis-related pain.
classified.rationale: This states a mechanistic relationship between obstruction and pain.

classified.text: Endometriosis and adenomyosis are more likely consequences or associated findings rather than the primary diagnosis causing primary amenorrhea.
classified.rationale: This interprets their role relative to the main syndrome.

classified.text: The single most likely diagnosis is an obstructive genital tract müllerian anomaly causing cryptomenorrhea.
classified.rationale: This identifies the diagnosis and its causal mechanism.

classified.text: The strongest specific fit among obstructive lesions is a transverse vaginal septum or upper vaginal agenesis or atresia.
classified.rationale: This selects the most likely obstructive lesion based on the findings.

classified.rationale: This reports a direct imaging description.

classified.rationale: This reports an anatomic/imaging finding.

classified.text: The retained blood in the right uterine horn explains the acute severe pain.
classified.rationale: This links retained blood to the acute pain episode.

classified.text: The best final diagnosis is transverse vaginal septum causing cryptomenorrhea and hematometra in the setting of a bicornuate unicollis uterus.
classified.rationale: This states the final diagnosis and the causal relationship to the symptoms.
